previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, recurrent urinary tract infections, and an indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted after a urine sample collected outpatient revealed growth of Klebsiella and Pseudomonas. He reported prior fevers and dysuria, but symptoms had resolved by admission and he remained asymptomatic. Infectious Disease was consulted and recommended against antibiotic treatment, as the findings were likely due to colonization rather than active infection, especially given a negative urine culture from a newly placed catheter. His sirolimus level was mildly elevated, but this was likely due to recent dosing; no adjustment was made, with plans to recheck as an outpatient. He remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no need for medication changes or procedures. He was discharged home with instructions to monitor for urinary symptoms and to follow up with urology regarding intermittent catheterization to reduce future infection risk.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo M s/p OLT in ___ who has had recurrent 
MDR UTIs and has multiple antibotic allergies and history of 
urosepsis who was sent in from clinic for eradication of 
resistant pseudomonal urinary colonizer.

#UTI: Patinet is asymptomatic, however it was felt that given 
his immunocompromised state as he is on sirolimus and had a 
history of urosepsis leading to ICU stay in early ___, that he 
would benefit from eradication with IV meropenem. Pt's prior 
urine cultures have grown several organisms including 
Klebsiella, E coli, and Pseudomonas, all sensitive to meropenem. 
He also has an indwelling foley for urinary retention. Upon 
presentation, Pt was seen by infectious diseases, who 
recommended started empiric treatment with meropenem given past 
species sensitivities, and discontinuing his foley catheter, 
which most likely was infected. It was initially believed that 
Pt would need to straight cath himself given his prior issues 
with urinary retention. However, that was not necessary as he 
has had relatively good urine output. He was provided with 
teaching on self-cath technique. Infectious diseases also 
recommended a prostate ultrasound to rule out prostate abscess 
as a potential cause of repeated UTIs. His prostate ultrasound 
on ___ showed now evidence of prostate abscess. Dr. ___ 
Transplant ___ Diseases felt that his history of 
difficult-to-treat UTIs warranted continuous ""suppressive"" 
antibiotics. The patient was discharged with his suggested 
regimen of fosfomycin (Monurol) 3g dissolved in water, po, 1x 
weekly and follow-up in his clinic in one week.

#Nutrition- patient reports having no problems with eating 
recently and has only been using the feeding tube as needed when 
he feels he hasn't eaten enough. Nutrition recommended Nutren 
2.0/Two Cal HN Full strength at 70 ml/hr, Residual Checks every 
4 hrs and hold for residual greater than 200 ml, flush with 30 
ml water before and after each feeding. This regimen was 
followed in the hospital. His home vitamin regimen was 
continued.

was continued on his home regimen regiment of po hydromorphone, 
oxycontin, fentanyl patch, and lidocaine patch without incident.
.

opium.

appropriate at 7.9. Continued home dose.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  NG tube placement.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is little change in the
appearance of the long intestinal tube that extends to the distal portion of
the third part of the duodenum.  Left lung is clear.  Chronic collapse of the
right lower lobe is again seen, accompanied by a small pleural effusion.

INDICATION:  Status post liver transplant and history of recurrent
multi-resistant UTIs, evaluate for perirectal or prostate abscess.

TECHNIQUE:  Prostate ultrasound.

FINDINGS:  The prostate measures 4.0 x 2.0 x 3.1 cm, corresponding to a
calculated prostatic volume of 13.1 cc.  There is mild BPH with central
echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing consistent with
calcifications or corpora amylacea.  No evidence of prostate abscess.  The
seminal vesicles are symmetric.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of prostate abscess.
